de35b_texts.topic: What the texts say about choosing and removing the sovereign CEO

claims.text: Land p.5 (block quote of Moldbug): 'a state is a business which owns a country'; negotiable shares, each yields a fraction of profit; 'Each share has one vote, and the shareholders elect a board, which hires and fires managers.' Residents are customers.

Land p.5-6 (his own summary): 'squash the democratic myth that a state belongs to the citizenry'; 'buy out the real stakeholders in sovereign power'; map 'the entire social landscape of political bribery (lobbying)' and convert privileges into 'fungible shares'; 'Insofar as voters are worth bribing ... their portion of sovereignty will be estimated with appropriate derision'

Land p.6: once converted into a '(freely transferable) shareholding in gov-corp', owners 'initiate rational corporate governance, beginning with the appointment of a CEO'; interests = 'maximization of long-term shareholder value'; 'no longer any need for residents (clients) to take any interest in politics whatsoever. In fact, to do so would be to exhibit semi-criminal proclivities'; complain to 'customer service function' and 'take their custom elsewhere'; 'No voice, free exit.'
Land p.6 quotes Patri Friedman: free exit 'so important that we've called it the only Universal Human Right'

Moldbug, 'Democracy as Adaptive Fiction' (25 Jul 2007): joint-stock form eliminates 'the hereditary principle which caused so many problems for so many monarchies'; 'Good Government as Good Customer Service' (25 May 2007): 'Fnargland is a business. Like any business, it has no reason at all to alienate its customers'; Patchwork Part 1 (13 Nov 2008): statelets 'each governed by its own joint-stock corporation without regard to the residents' opinions'; 'If residents don't like their government, they can and should move.'; 'The design is all exit, no voice.'; Gentle Introduction 9d: 'a qualified administrator - an experienced corporate CEO, perhaps'

NYT 18 Jan 2025: Marchese contrasted Marcus Aurelius and Nero and listed 20th-century dictators; Yarvin: 'Your question is the most important question of all', then discussed the 20th century and the Holocaust; no mechanism for removing a bad ruler given in the exchange
NYT 2025: on CEOs, Yarvin said the median Fortune 500 CEO would outperform Washington: 'just pick one at random and put him or her in charge of Washington'

NYT 2025: on voting, 'I believe that voting is providing this almost pornographic stimulus'; voting gives status and relevance like a sports team; 'what does this power mean to you is really the most important question'
NYT 2025: an American monarch 'you have to be the president of all Americans'; Trump voters 'elected as they think a revolution'

de35b_systems.topic: How real systems choose and remove rulers

claims.text: 21 June 2017: King Salman's decree made Mohammed bin Salman (31) crown prince, removing Mohammed bin Nayef (57) as heir and interior minister; Allegiance Council of senior Al Saud members endorsed 31 of 34

24 Jan 2006: Kuwait's 65-member parliament voted unanimously (two-thirds needed) at the government's request to remove Emir Sheikh Saad al-Abdullah al-Sabah, who had 'lost his health capability' to exercise his prerogatives; abdication letter arrived after the vote; cabinet led by PM Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad took head-of-state functions and he became emir

11 March 2018: China's NPC voted 2,958 to 2 with 3 abstentions to remove the two-consecutive-term limit on the presidency set in 1982 under Deng to prevent a repeat of Mao-era one-man rule; Xi had not named a successor at the end of his first term

OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman on 17 Nov 2023, saying he was 'not consistently candid in his communications with the board'; nearly all of about 800 employees signed a letter threatening to leave for Microsoft unless the board resigned; agreement for his return announced 21 Nov 2023 with a new board (Taylor, Summers, D'Angelo)

Didius Julianus became Roman emperor 28 March 193 after winning an auction for the Praetorian Guard's support by offering the largest donative, outbidding Sulpicianus; reigned about two months; killed when the Danube legions under Septimius Severus entered Italy (June 193)

East India Company: shareholders (Court of Proprietors) elected the 24-member Court of Directors, six rotating out each April; after Pitt's India Act 1784 a parliamentary Board of Control held controlling authority and proprietors could no longer annul directors' policies; Court of Directors abolished 1858

Venice 1268 doge protocol: ten rounds alternating lot (30, 40, 25, 45) and election (9, 12, 9, 11, 41); the final 41 needed 25 votes; lot made it hard for bribers to predict the electors (Mowbray and Gollmann 2007)
